newsitem.title: CANADA: RENAISSANCE FALLS AFTER WEAKER Q2 RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: RENAISSANCE FALLS AFTER WEAKER Q2 RESULTS.

text.p: Shares in Renaissance Energy Ltd slid again in busy volume on Tuesday after the company released its second quarter results.
The sell-off came despite a well-publicized warning from Renaissance Chief Executive Clayton Woitas last month that 1997 production and cash flow would fall short of forecasts.
That warning caused a deep meltdown in the stock as investors were driven away by one of the Canadian oil industry leaders production woes.
Renaissance on Tuesday was trading down 1.35 in Toronto to 35.85. Earlier, it fell to as low as 35.55.
Renaissance reported second-quarter cash flow of C$113 million or C$0.98 a share, down from C$131 million or C$1.24 a share during the same period last year.
Earnings in the period slipped to C$18 million or C$0.16 a share from C$46 million or C$0.42 a share in the second quarter of 1996.
"The market reacts to facts," said Peter Linder, analyst with CIBC Wood Gundy. "Even though it's anticipated, they see the numbers and they react."

Renaissance said its oil production averaged 79,175 barrels a day in the second quarter, up from 64,264 in the same period last year. Gas output averaged 432 million cubic feet a day, up from 384 million.

Woitas said in July that severely wet spring weather and other operational delays hampered the company's ability to drill and grow its production to forecast 1997 levels. Oil output expectations were scaled back to 85,000 barrels a day for the full year from the previous projection of 92,500.
Lower average natural gas and crude oil prices compared to last year for would also translate into weaker returns for the year for Renaissance.

"With a 15-20 percent lower commodity price, production is going to have to be 15-20 percent higher just to stay even," said Linder, who rates the stock a "hold" with what he calls a "very kind" C$40 12-month target.
"They also issued some stock last September, so there's more shares outstanding in 1997 than in '96. There's some dilution there."
Meanwhile, Renaissance said it was on track to spend C$800 million in 1997 drilling 1,700 to 1,800 wells. It also planned to tie in about 150 shut-in gas wells in Alberta's Athabasca region.
